thesis: CLEAR Secure reported Q3 2026 today (8-K), and the stock rose about 23.8% to $59.13 on 5.1x volume. Revenue grew 27.8% to $292.9M, total bookings grew 24.4% to $323.5M, the adjusted EBITDA margin was 35.5%, and Q4 revenue guidance of $299-302M sits above consensus. The counter-case is structural and not resolved. Free cash flow was -$103.8M because the company settled about $315M of accrued partnership liabilities, and it will make quarterly partnership-liability payments starting Q1 2027. That is an ongoing cash claim on the airport and airline model. Coverage also flags an elevated valuation. Legal: the 2024-25 law-firm investigation notices led to no filed suit that this run found, and the 2023 TSA scrutiny has no scheduled next step. This run found no restatement or equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: Bookings growth slows or partnership payments materially compress free cash flow, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$47.76).

thesis: Viridian reported Q3 2026 today (8-K and 10-Q), and the stock rose about 15.5% to $29.05 on 5.0x volume. In the first full quarter since its June 26 FDA approval for thyroid eye disease, Lumvoa (veligrotug) produced $24.7M of net revenue, against a ~$19.2M estimate, with more than 100 patients on therapy. The company holds $955.2M in cash and says that plus Lumvoa and elegrobart revenue funds the plan through profitability. The elegrobart BLA is on track for Q1 2027. The counter-case is named but not resolved: this is one early launch quarter against the incumbent TED therapy, and the GAAP loss remains large at -$3.86 per share. This run found no 2026 equity offering, no litigation and no restatement. This is medium.
invalidation: Lumvoa patient adds or revenue stall in coming quarters, an elegrobart BLA delay, or a new equity raise, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$25.15).

thesis: Flywire reported Q3 2026 on Nov 3 after the close (8-K), and the stock rose about 13.8% to $21.80 on 4.7x volume, a new 52-week high. Revenue grew 25.1% to $250.3M, adjusted EPS of $0.68 beat the ~$0.50 estimate, and FY2026 FX-neutral revenue growth guidance was raised by 2 points with adjusted EBITDA margin guidance up 30bp. The counter-case is structural and not resolved. Student visa and permit restrictions on international education are the same issue at the center of a 2025 securities class action (E.D.N.Y., class period Feb 2024-Feb 2025), which this run found with no scheduled ruling. One raised guide doesn't settle that policy exposure. This run found no restatement or equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: Visa or permit restrictions hit education volumes or guidance is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$19.15).

thesis: Fortune Brands reported Q3 2026 on Nov 3 (8-K). Sales fell 3.1%, operating income fell 24.6%, and GAAP EPS of $0.42 included a $0.47 impairment. Adjusted EPS of $1.14 beat consensus, but it was helped by a $0.28 tax benefit and $0.14 of tariff refunds, and Water segment margins fell as pricing failed to offset inflation. Management expects lower Q4 revenue, and the company is selling Fiberon for $160M with a further $175-205M impairment expected, exiting China commercial operations, and targeting $70M of SG&A savings. The CEO seat turned over twice in 2026, with Jesse Singh appointed June 29 amid an activist stake. The stock rose 3.4% on 4.4x volume, but the underlying results are weak and supported by one-time items. This is low; avoid.
invalidation: Q4 shows Water margins recovering and organic sales stabilizing under the restructuring.

thesis: Performance Food Group reported fiscal Q1 2027 today and rose about 13.6% to $109.62 on 4.3x volume. Adjusted EPS of $1.32 beat the ~$1.27-1.28 consensus and rose 12%, revenue of about $18.0B was in line (+5.5%), and full-year guidance was reiterated. But next-quarter revenue guidance came in about 1.7% below consensus, and the size of the move is out of proportion to an in-line print with unchanged guidance. Legal and governance: the 2025 US Foods merger talks ended, and Sachem Head holds a board seat under a 2025 cooperation agreement. This run found no litigation, restatement or equity raise. With a modest beat offset by soft next-quarter revenue guidance, the read is mixed, so this is low.
invalidation: Revenue reaccelerates above guidance with full-year guidance raised.

thesis: Stanley Black & Decker reported Q3 2026 today (8-K and 10-Q) and rose about 13.0% to $118.24 on 4.3x volume, a new 52-week high. Organic sales grew 4% on 6% volume growth despite a 2% price decline, free cash flow was about $585M, the company raised its 2026 EPS and free-cash-flow outlook, and it authorized a new $1B buyback. The counter-case is named but not resolved: roughly $0.67 per share of the $2.31 adjusted EPS came from net tariff refunds that won't recur, so the underlying beat is smaller than the headline. Legal: a DOJ Consumer Product Safety Act civil suit over utility bars and miter saws, filed Dec 2025, has no scheduled step identified. The 2023 SEC perquisites order was not a restatement. This is medium.
invalidation: Volume growth fades once tariff refunds roll off and the raised outlook is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$104.62).

thesis: GXO reported Q3 2026 on Nov 3 after the close and rose about 9.4% to $56.93 on 4.1x volume. Revenue grew 5.7% to $3.6B (organic +6.4%), new business wins rose 34% to $375M, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed. Against that, adjusted EBITDA was flat at $251M, operating income fell to $96M from $118M, and free cash flow fell to $85M from $187M. Coverage was split on the after-hours reaction. An Investor Day on Nov 16 is a pending catalyst. This run found no litigation, restatement or equity raise, and CEO Patrick Kelleher has served since August 2025. With growth and wins offset by flat EBITDA and weaker cash generation, the read is mixed, so this is low.
invalidation: The Nov 16 Investor Day targets show EBITDA and free-cash-flow growth catching up with revenue.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF fell about 9.3% to $12.83 on roughly normal volume (27.2M against a 25.1M average). This run's search found no company disclosure or news explaining the drop, and MarketBeat shows only older analyst items. The stock remains above the ~$12.12 pre-report invalidation level. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, the Stelco/Canada dispute continues, and leverage is high. An unexplained 9% drop is price action, not a fundamental change, but it leaves the stock only about 6% above invalidation. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 6.0% to $38.22 on 1.6x volume; this run found no new company disclosure, and Citi raised its target to $56 on Oct 28. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results: brepocitinib met the primary and all key secondary endpoints in non-infectious uveitis. The drug is already approved for dermatomyositis as Lisraya. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved, and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).
sources: Yahoo Finance (ROIV quote, Nov 9 earnings): https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ROIV/

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene rose about 12.6% to $75.99 on 3.1x volume, a new 52-week high, after three firms raised their outlooks, including Truist reiterating Buy with an $82 target. The close is now well above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, so the price invalidation that kept this low is no longer met. The thesis rests on the Oct 27 Q3 report (8-K): adjusted EPS of $0.58 against a ~$0.07-0.10 consensus and full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised above $5.20. Analyst upgrades are not independent confirmation, and the counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of 2026 adjusted EPS from non-recurring items, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. Those cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal). NWL rose about 4.0% to $5.855; this run found no new company disclosure. This run's research surfaced more of the Oct 30 Q3 report. Alongside 3.7% sales growth, a 90bp normalized margin gain to 9.8% and a full-year sales outlook raised to +2-3%, the company cut its operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M on pension and factoring effects and flagged about $220M of inflation headwinds. It also took a $101M impairment, and full-year adjusted EPS was only maintained. Analysts are split: UBS raised its target to $5.75, while Morgan Stanley and Citi cut theirs. Taken together, the operating gains are offset by a sharply lower cash outlook and cost headwinds, so the evidence is mixed and this is low. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 1 trading day ago), and these are facts from the same Oct 30 report the entry thesis relied on, not new facts, so the direction stays long. The stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).

thesis: Held position (opened today, Nov 4, on the Nov 3 proposal). After the close today, Janus Living launched a public offering of 25M Class A-1 shares, plus a 3.75M-share underwriter option, to fund acquisitions, repay its revolver and for general purposes. That is about 27% of its ~92M-share float, and it follows a 16M-share offering priced at $29 in August, within the last ~90 days, which the entry thesis wrongly reported as absent. Shares were quoted near $29.00 after hours, against a $30.06 close. This is a dilution_risk-level fact, and it is the specific form of the entry thesis's named counter-case: an externally managed, Healthpeak-controlled REIT issuing equity repeatedly, which disadvantages existing holders. Under the rubric the thesis would now be low, below the bar this position was opened on. The early-exit guard applies (opened today), and it is satisfied: the offering announcement is dated Nov 4, after the Nov 3 entry thesis. Exit.
